title: Diffusion Sampling Path Tells More: An Efficient Plug-and-Play Strategy for Sample Filtering
role: Shows the squared length of the score path (sum over steps of ||cond - uncond||^2) ranks seeds by quality with no training; a length signal any score-path encoder must control for
reads: Per-step l2 norm of the conditional minus unconditional model output at the same x_t (flattened; times sigma_t for SDXL and FLUX; channel-averaged matrix norm for EDM2); direction discarded
combines: G_t = ||S(x_t; c) - S(x_t; null)||_2, summed as squares over the first tau steps (E_tau:T); seeds below a percentile threshold are stopped early
adding: not addressed; one condition against the empty condition only, and no theory for why ASD tracks density
noise_and_seed: ASD ranks seeds of one prompt; 10k ImageNet samples over 50 classes, 4 of 20 or 4 of 50 seeds per GenEval prompt, three repeats averaged with no spread reported
timesteps: first 20 of 32 steps match the full sum on ImageNet (PickScore 20.61 both); GenEval counting peaks at the first 10 of 50 steps; G_t said to shrink in later steps
unseen: no held-out concepts (nothing trained); composition tested on GenEval and DPG-Bench: SD1.5 two-object 0.354 to 0.518 by keeping 4 of 50 seeds, counting falls in several settings
headline: GenEval two-object 0.5177 vs 0.3540 random (fraction, SD1.5, guidance 5, 4 of 50 seeds by ASD); ImageNet PickScore 20.61 top 10% vs 20.38 all (EDM2-S)
suggests: (inferred) Path length alone ranks seeds, so a score-path encoder should see per-step-normalised d_t, and the sum-lands-on-joint test should first compare product and joint path lengths per seed

disagreements.claim: ASD filtering yields consistent improvements across all categories and guidance scales
disagreements.source: paper itself, p. 8 text vs Tables 2 and 4
disagreements.paper_says: Counting falls from 0.3359 to 0.3235 (SD1.5, guidance 5, 4 of 20) and from 0.4094 to 0.3250 (SDXL, guidance 5, 4 of 50); SDXL guidance 9 overall falls from 0.5625 to 0.5510 with 4 of 50

disagreements.claim: +46% gain on two-object relationship prompts from early filtering
disagreements.paper_says: The 46% is the 4-of-50 full-ASD row (0.3540 to 0.5177); early filtering at tau = 10 gives 0.3801 (+7%). GenEval's two-object category tests co-occurrence of two objects, not relationships (inferred)

disagreements.claim: a strong correlation between ASD and high-density regions
disagreements.paper_says: No correlation coefficient is printed; the evidence is a binned log-linear plot over 50 ASD bins on a 2D toy and density-curve figures on ImageNet

disagreements.claim: the score difference G_t is one defined quantity
disagreements.paper_says: EDM2 uses a channel-averaged matrix two-norm without sigma_t scaling, SD1.5 a flattened l2 norm, SDXL and FLUX a flattened l2 norm times sigma_t, so G_t is in different units across models (inferred)
